raw:
---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: security
TITLE: Arbitrary file read with no path validation or sandboxing
DESCRIPTION: `parse_config` accepts any string path and reads it via `Path(path).read_text()`. An attacker or misconfigured caller can supply paths like `/etc/passwd`, `../../secrets.env`, or UNC paths on Windows. There is no restriction to a safe directory, no symlink check, and no canonicalization.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Resolve the path with `Path(path).resolve()` and assert it is inside an expected base directory before reading; reject or raise on paths that escape the sandbox.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Bare `partition(":")` breaks on values containing colons
DESCRIPTION: `line.partition(":")` splits on the *first* colon only, so a value like `url: https://example.com` yields `key="url"`, `value="https://example.com"` — the double-slash is preserved but any value of the form `key: host:port` (e.g., `db: localhost:5432`) will produce `value="localhost"` and silently discard `:5432`. The remainder after the first colon is always lost because `partition` is used but only `_` (the separator) is discarded while the third element is taken as the full value — actually this part is fine; however a value like `time: 12:30:00` loses `:00`.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `line.split(":", 1)` and take index 1 as the raw value, which is equivalent but makes the intent explicit; document that colons in values are preserved, and add a test for `hh:mm:ss`-style values.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Empty key silently inserted when line starts with colon
DESCRIPTION: A line like `: value` passes the `not line` check, and `key.strip()` produces an empty string `""`. This empty-string key is inserted into `config` without error. Later code that iterates keys or looks up expected keys will silently receive an unexpected entry, or a subsequent `: other` line will overwrite it with no warning.
SUGGESTED_FIX: After stripping, check `if not key: continue` (or raise) before inserting into the dict.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: high
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Line with no colon stores entire line as value under empty key
DESCRIPTION: If a line contains no `:`, `partition(":")` returns `(line, "", "")`. `key` becomes the full line content and `value` becomes `""`. This silently adds a key whose name is the raw line text mapped to an empty string, rather than raising a parse error for a malformed entry.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check that `_` (the separator returned by `partition`) is non-empty before proceeding; if it is empty, log a warning or raise `ValueError` for the malformed line.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Negative integers not coerced — stored as strings
DESCRIPTION: `value.isdigit()` returns `False` for negative numbers like `-42` because `-` is not a digit character. The regex below only matches floats (`-?\d+\.\d+`). So `-42` falls through to the string branch and is stored as `"-42"` instead of `int(-42)`. This silent type mismatch will cause `TypeError` or wrong comparisons downstream.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Replace `value.isdigit()` with `re.match(r"^-?\d+$", value)` (or a `try/except int()` conversion) to handle negative integers.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Scientific-notation and edge-case floats silently stored as strings
DESCRIPTION: Values like `1e10`, `1.0e-3`, `.5`, `1.`, or `inf` do not match `^-?\d+\.\d+$` and fall through to the string branch. Callers expecting numeric types will receive strings for valid numeric literals, causing silent downstream type errors.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Attempt `float(value)` inside a `try/except ValueError` as a fallback after the digit check, covering the full range of Python float literals.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: Duplicate keys silently overwritten without warning
DESCRIPTION: If the same key appears multiple times in the file, each occurrence overwrites the previous value with no diagnostic. The caller has no way to know that data was silently lost, which can mask misconfigured files or injection of a second key after a legitimate one.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check `if key in config` before assignment and either raise `ValueError` or emit a warning (via `warnings.warn` or a logger) indicating the duplicate key and line number.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: observability
TITLE: Silent swallowing of all parse exceptions discards error context
DESCRIPTION: Both the outer `except Exception: return config` and the inner `except Exception: pass` discard all error information. A permissions error, encoding error, or unexpected crash is indistinguishable from a normal empty config. The `line_num` variable is computed but never used in any diagnostic.
SUGGESTED_FIX: At minimum log the exception and line number; for the file-read failure, consider re-raising or returning a sentinel so callers can distinguish "file not found" from "empty config".

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: No encoding specified; fails on non-UTF-8 config files
DESCRIPTION: `Path.read_text()` uses the platform default encoding (locale-dependent on Windows, typically UTF-8 on Linux). A config file saved in Latin-1 or UTF-16 will raise `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is silently swallowed, returning an empty dict with no indication of the failure.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Pass an explicit `encoding=` parameter (e.g., `encoding="utf-8"`) and optionally `errors="replace"` or handle `UnicodeDecodeError` separately with a clear error message.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: `merge_configs` does shallow update; nested dict values are not deep-merged
DESCRIPTION: `base.update(override)` replaces top-level keys wholesale. If both configs contain a key whose value is a dict (which this parser does not currently produce, but callers may extend it to), the base dict is silently replaced rather than merged. This is a latent design flaw that will break if the parser is extended.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document explicitly that only flat configs are supported and that nested structures are not deep-merged, or implement a recursive `deep_merge` helper.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: medium
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `isdigit()` returns True for Unicode digit characters
DESCRIPTION: `str.isdigit()` returns `True` for Unicode superscript digits (e.g., `²`, `³`) and other Unicode numeric characters. `int("²")` then raises `ValueError`, which is silently caught, leaving the key absent from the config without any indication.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `re.match(r"^\d+$", value)` with ASCII-only digits, or guard the `int()` call with a `try/except` and log the failure.

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: Inline comment stripping not implemented; `#` in values is preserved literally
DESCRIPTION: A line like `name: Alice # admin user` stores the value `"Alice # admin user"` rather than `"Alice"`. Users accustomed to YAML or INI conventions will be surprised; the docstring implies YAML-like behaviour but trailing comments are silently included in values.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Document that inline comments are not supported, or strip everything from ` #` onward after splitting on `:` (taking care not to strip `#` characters that are genuinely part of a value, e.g., hex color codes).

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: edge-case
TITLE: No maximum file size guard; large files read entirely into memory
DESCRIPTION: `read_text()` loads the entire file into a single string before processing. A maliciously large or accidentally huge file will exhaust memory, potentially causing an OOM kill or swap thrash with no graceful error.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Check `Path(path).stat().st_size` before reading and raise or warn if it exceeds a reasonable limit (e.g., 1 MB for a config file).

---FINDING---
SEVERITY: low
CATEGORY: logic
TITLE: `line_num` is computed but never surfaced in any output
DESCRIPTION: `enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1)` tracks line numbers, but `line_num` is never referenced — not in error messages, not in the returned dict, not in logging. Its computation is wasted and misleads future maintainers into thinking errors are already attributed to source lines.
SUGGESTED_FIX: Either use `line_num` in error/warning messages, or remove `enumerate` and iterate directly over `text.splitlines()` to avoid the false implication.

---END---

SUGGESTED_FIX: Use `line.split(":", 1)` and take index 1 as the raw value, which is equivalent but makes the intent explicit; document that colons in values are preserved, and add a test for `hh:mm:ss`-style values.

findings.title: Empty key silently inserted when line starts with colon
findings.description: A line like `: value` passes the `not line` check, and `key.strip()` produces an empty string `""`. This empty-string key is inserted into `config` without error. Later code that iterates keys or looks up expected keys will silently receive an unexpected entry, or a subsequent `: other` line will overwrite it with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: After stripping, check `if not key: continue` (or raise) before inserting into the dict.

findings.title: Line with no colon stores entire line as value under empty key
findings.description: If a line contains no `:`, `partition(":")` returns `(line, "", "")`. `key` becomes the full line content and `value` becomes `""`. This silently adds a key whose name is the raw line text mapped to an empty string, rather than raising a parse error for a malformed entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Check that `_` (the separator returned by `partition`) is non-empty before proceeding; if it is empty, log a warning or raise `ValueError` for the malformed line.

findings.title: Negative integers not coerced — stored as strings
findings.description: `value.isdigit()` returns `False` for negative numbers like `-42` because `-` is not a digit character. The regex below only matches floats (`-?\d+\.\d+`). So `-42` falls through to the string branch and is stored as `"-42"` instead of `int(-42)`. This silent type mismatch will cause `TypeError` or wrong comparisons downstream.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `value.isdigit()` with `re.match(r"^-?\d+$", value)` (or a `try/except int()` conversion) to handle negative integers.

findings.title: Scientific-notation and edge-case floats silently stored as strings
findings.description: Values like `1e10`, `1.0e-3`, `.5`, `1.`, or `inf` do not match `^-?\d+\.\d+$` and fall through to the string branch. Callers expecting numeric types will receive strings for valid numeric literals, causing silent downstream type errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Attempt `float(value)` inside a `try/except ValueError` as a fallback after the digit check, covering the full range of Python float literals.

findings.title: Duplicate keys silently overwritten without warning
findings.description: If the same key appears multiple times in the file, each occurrence overwrites the previous value with no diagnostic. The caller has no way to know that data was silently lost, which can mask misconfigured files or injection of a second key after a legitimate one.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `if key in config` before assignment and either raise `ValueError` or emit a warning (via `warnings.warn` or a logger) indicating the duplicate key and line number.

findings.title: Silent swallowing of all parse exceptions discards error context
findings.description: Both the outer `except Exception: return config` and the inner `except Exception: pass` discard all error information. A permissions error, encoding error, or unexpected crash is indistinguishable from a normal empty config. The `line_num` variable is computed but never used in any diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum log the exception and line number; for the file-read failure, consider re-raising or returning a sentinel so callers can distinguish "file not found" from "empty config".

findings.title: No encoding specified; fails on non-UTF-8 config files
findings.description: `Path.read_text()` uses the platform default encoding (locale-dependent on Windows, typically UTF-8 on Linux). A config file saved in Latin-1 or UTF-16 will raise `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is silently swallowed, returning an empty dict with no indication of the failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass an explicit `encoding=` parameter (e.g., `encoding="utf-8"`) and optionally `errors="replace"` or handle `UnicodeDecodeError` separately with a clear error message.

findings.title: `merge_configs` does shallow update; nested dict values are not deep-merged
findings.description: `base.update(override)` replaces top-level keys wholesale. If both configs contain a key whose value is a dict (which this parser does not currently produce, but callers may extend it to), the base dict is silently replaced rather than merged. This is a latent design flaw that will break if the parser is extended.
findings.suggested_fix: Document explicitly that only flat configs are supported and that nested structures are not deep-merged, or implement a recursive `deep_merge` helper.

findings.title: `isdigit()` returns True for Unicode digit characters
findings.description: `str.isdigit()` returns `True` for Unicode superscript digits (e.g., `²`, `³`) and other Unicode numeric characters. `int("²")` then raises `ValueError`, which is silently caught, leaving the key absent from the config without any indication.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `re.match(r"^\d+$", value)` with ASCII-only digits, or guard the `int()` call with a `try/except` and log the failure.

findings.title: Inline comment stripping not implemented; `#` in values is preserved literally
findings.description: A line like `name: Alice # admin user` stores the value `"Alice # admin user"` rather than `"Alice"`. Users accustomed to YAML or INI conventions will be surprised; the docstring implies YAML-like behaviour but trailing comments are silently included in values.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that inline comments are not supported, or strip everything from ` #` onward after splitting on `:` (taking care not to strip `#` characters that are genuinely part of a value, e.g., hex color codes).

findings.title: No maximum file size guard; large files read entirely into memory
findings.description: `read_text()` loads the entire file into a single string before processing. A maliciously large or accidentally huge file will exhaust memory, potentially causing an OOM kill or swap thrash with no graceful error.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `Path(path).stat().st_size` before reading and raise or warn if it exceeds a reasonable limit (e.g., 1 MB for a config file).

findings.title: `line_num` is computed but never surfaced in any output
findings.description: `enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1)` tracks line numbers, but `line_num` is never referenced — not in error messages, not in the returned dict, not in logging. Its computation is wasted and misleads future maintainers into thinking errors are already attributed to source lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Either use `line_num` in error/warning messages, or remove `enumerate` and iterate directly over `text.splitlines()` to avoid the false implication.
